title: In Situ (S)TEM Investigation of Degradation Processes of Undoped and Doped Mn-rich High-voltage Cathodes
content: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are crucial energy storage devices due to their high energy density and long cycle life. Among various cathode materials like LiCoO2 and Ni-rich NMC, high-voltage spinel LiMn1.5Ni0.5O4 (LMNO) has been advantageous for its cost-effectiveness and superb cycling performance [1]. However, this material may undergo structural degradation and capacity fading, particularly while operating under high voltages (≥ 4.9V) [2, 3]. In this study, an in situ TEM open-cell approach was used to investigate the structural evolution and electrochemical performance of pristine and tungsten diselenide (WSe2)-doped LMNO cathodes during delithiation.
